rules.name: Resolve caller revisions safely before using them in git operations
rules.content: Trace caller-supplied revision strings to git invocations. Resolve them to commit IDs using git rev-parse --verify --end-of-options, reject resolution failures, and pass only resolved IDs to subsequent git commands. The resolver itself necessarily receives the revision after --end-of-options.

rules.name: Read git path listings with NUL delimiters
rules.content: For git commands listing file paths, verify use of -z and parsing of NUL-separated raw paths rather than newline splitting or quoted-path suffix checks.
rules.goodExamples:
out, err := exec.Command("git", "diff", "--name-only", "-z", base, head).Output()
paths := strings.Split(strings.TrimSuffix(string(out), "\x00"), "\x00")
_ = paths; _ = err
rules.badExamples:
out, err := exec.Command("git", "diff", "--name-only", base, head).Output()
paths := strings.Split(string(out), "\n")
_ = paths; _ = err

rules.name: Do not weaken tests to obtain a green build
rules.content: Review test changes for removed assertions, deleted tests, added skips, or added nolint suppressions used to bypass failures. If a test is claimed to be wrong, require the pull request to explain the correction. Do not treat deliberately weak source strings used as referee fixtures as weakened executable tests.

rules.name: Do not add third-party dependencies without the documented human exception
rules.content: Inspect go.mod changes for new dependencies. The default is standard-library-only; an exception requires that the standard library cannot do the job and that an issue with human approval exists.
rules.badExamples:
module github.com/bettersandeep/yantra

go 1.23

require github.com/stretchr/testify v1.9.0 // added without approval

rules.name: Commands must exit with code 2 when a check cannot run
rules.content: Trace check errors through command entry points and verify that inability to run the check produces exit status 2, not clean status 0 or findings status 1.

rules.name: Checks must fail closed on unreadable, unparseable, or unsupported input
rules.content: Inspect check input handling, parsing, and unsupported-input branches in internal/referee, cmd/yantra, and future checks. Each inability to inspect an input must return an error rather than skip it or report clean.

rules.name: Bug fixes must include a regression test that fails before the fix
rules.content: For each bug or review-finding fix, inspect the added test case and confirm that it fails against the pre-fix implementation and passes against the corrected implementation.
rules.badExamples:
// Fix option injection, but add no test exercising an option-like revision.
base, err := resolve(baseRev)
